message.content:
Design a detailed implementation architecture for a major 3D/dark-theme overhaul of a Next.js 16 real estate site at /home/cis/windows/realstate. DO NOT re-explore broadly — I'm giving you comprehensive findings below. Read only specific files you need to verify a design decision.

## The user's request (verbatim intent)
Convert the site to a premium DARK theme with heavy 3D/animation. Specifically:
1. On first visit, a **full-screen onboarding gate**: a 3D human girl real-estate-agent model greets the visitor **with voice**, asks their name; visitor types name into an input and clicks "Let's Go"; then the main site opens.
2. The model's **eyes/head follow the mouse pointer** (look right when cursor is right).
3. Main site has **premium 3D animations**: a scroll-driven **building construction sequence from pillars → finished tower**.
4. A **scrollable 3D apartment interior walkthrough** (room interiors, high quality).
5. Aesthetic quality is the priority — **the user explicitly said NOT to focus on performance/load time**.

## Decisions already locked by the user
- **Avatar**: Ready Player Me (free GLB, ships ARKit 52 blendshapes → real lip-sync + eye/eyelid control).
- **Voice**: Pre-recorded ElevenLabs MP3s committed as static assets (fixed script, zero runtime cost/latency).
- **3D scenes**: Procedural Three.js geometry (no sourced GLB for building/interior) — instanced columns/slabs/facade driven by scroll; interior built procedurally from existing floor-plan data.
- **Scope**: Whole site dark theme (token-driven), 3D showpieces concentrated on home + project detail, delivered in phases.

## Verified codebase facts (trust these; do not re-derive)

**Stack**: Next.js 16.3.0 App Router, React 19.2.8, Tailwind v4 (CSS-first `@theme inline`, no tailwind.config), TypeScript strict. Installed: three@0.185, @react-three/fiber@9.7, @react-three/drei@10.7, gsap@3.15 + @gsap/react (useGSAP NEVER imported), lenis@1.3.26, framer-motion@13, pannellum, maplibre-gl, zod@4, react-hook-form, resend, embla. NOT installed: @react-three/postprocessing, next-themes, any state library, any speech/voice lib. `node_modules` is NOT installed yet. `next.config.ts` is completely empty.

**Theming (app/globals.css, 297 lines)**:
- `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *));` at line 5 and a complete `.dark { ... }` token block at line 128 ALREADY EXIST but are **dead code** — nothing ever adds the `.dark` class. Zero `dark:` variants in any .tsx. No next-themes. No `prefers-color-scheme`.
- Tokens are `@theme inline`, mapping `--color-*` → raw vars on `:root`. So **flipping `:root` values alone re-themes every semantic utility**.
- Raw palette: `--charcoal #141414`, `--charcoal-2 #1a1a1a`, `--ivory #f5f1e8`, `--cream #ede7da`, `--gold #b99c6b`, `--gold-soft #c9ae7c`, `--bronze #7a5a33`, `--forest #243b34`, `--navy #0a192f` (defined, NEVER used — free slot), `--stone #6b6b6b`, `--stone-2 #9a9a9a`.
- **Semantic classes convert for free (~265 occurrences)**: text-muted-foreground (149), border-border (73), text-foreground (22), divide-border (13), border-foreground (12), bg-card (5), text-destructive (4), bg-background (2), ring-ring (1).
- **Raw brand classes must be remapped (~200 occurrences)**: text-bronze (64 — at 1.9:1 on charcoal this is a hard WCAG FAIL, top priority), text-ivory (36), bg-charcoal (20), bg-cream/50 (15 — the standard alternating-section tint, becomes muddy tan over charcoal), text-stone-2 (13), text-gold-soft (8), text-charcoal (8), bg-forest (6 — nearly invisible on charcoal, 1.5:1), bg-gold (5), border-charcoal (4), border-bronze (4, used as focus:border-bronze → invisible focus risk), bg-ivory (3), plus ~20 one-offs with opacity modifiers. Also `border-white/10` ×3, `border-white/25` ×1, `accent-[var(--bronze)]` ×2.
- **The `bg-charcoal`+`text-ivory` "inverted emphasis" device (20 sites) LOSES ITS MEANING on a dark page** — needs replacing with an elevated-surface + gold-hairline treatment. Needs new `--surface-2`/`--surface-3` elevation tokens.
- `components/layout/site-footer.tsx` is ALREADY fully dark (charcoal/stone-2/gold-soft/white-10) — it is the de-facto design reference for the target theme. Risk: it stops separating from `main` once the page is also charcoal.
- Hard-coded hexes NOT following tokens (must hand-edit): hero-scene.tsx (#141414,#f5f1e8,#b99c6b,#2a2622,#1a1a1a), master-plan-3d.tsx (same set +#8c6a3f), placeholder-visual.tsx gradient, pannellum-tour.tsx backgroundColor [0.08,0.08,0.08], opengraph-image.tsx (already dark, fine).
- Components reading tokens via `var()` in SVG/JS: floor-plan-viewer.tsx, corridor-map.tsx, progress-timeline.tsx, emi-calculator.tsx.
- `site-header.tsx`: two visual states via `solid = scrolled || menuOpen || !overDarkHero` where `overDarkHero = useSelectedLayoutSegment() === null`. **On a dark site this duality collapses** — both states look the same; differentiator must become backdrop-blur + hairline.
- `whatsapp-fab.tsx` uses `bg-forest ring-8 ring-forest/20` — the glow is invisible on charcoal.
- Skip link in layout.tsx is hardcoded `bg-charcoal text-ivory` — invisible on a charcoal page.
- `<html>` has NO `dark` class, NO `suppressHydrationWarning`, no `color-scheme`, no `themeColor` metadata.
- `.rule` class defined, used 0 times. `@import "shadcn/tailwind.css"` — package not present, no components/ui/ dir exists.
- tailwind-merge v3.6 has NO custom config, so it doesn't know `text-h3` is a size and `text-bronze` is a color — custom-class conflicts may not dedupe. README warns about exactly this for `.eyebrow`.

**Existing 3D/motion machinery (REUSE, don't rebuild)**:
- `lib/webgl.ts`: `hasWebGL()` creates a real probe context then releases via WEBGL_lose_context. `isLowCapabilityDevice()` returns true on `(pointer:coarse)` OR `(max-width:1023px)` OR `deviceMemory<4` OR `hardwareConcurrency<4`. `shouldRenderWebGL(reducedMotion) = !reducedMotion && !isLowCapability && hasWebGL()`. **CRITICAL: this refuses WebGL on EVERY phone and every viewport <1024px.** A mandatory full-screen 3D gate cannot use it as-is.
- `components/webgl-boundary.tsx`: class error boundary, `getDerivedStateFromError` → renders `fallback ?? null`. No reset, no `webglcontextlost` listener (that event doesn't throw so it isn't caught).
- `components/lazy-mount.tsx`: one-shot IntersectionObserver, `rootMargin="400px"` default, exports `LazyMount` + `Skeleton({className})`.
- **The canonical two-gate 3D mount** is `components/projects/master-plan.tsx`: shouldRenderWebGL → IntersectionObserver(rootMargin 300px) → requestIdleCallback → setAllowed → `<WebGLBoundary><MasterPlan3D/></WebGLBoundary>`, with `dynamic(..., {ssr:false, loading:<Skeleton/>})`.
- **The deferred-wrapper convention**: `components/**/deferred-*.tsx` = `"use client"` + `dynamic(() => import(...).then(m => m.X), {ssr:false, loading:<height-reserving pulse>})` + thin prop-forwarding wrapper. Four exist: deferred-floor-plans, deferred-brochure, deferred-emi-calculator, deferred-enquiry-form.
- `components/hero/scroll-frame-sequence.tsx` (207 lines) is the CURRENT hero: canvas-2D image-sequence scrub over 36 WebP frames. **Progress is sampled inside a permanent rAF loop reading getBoundingClientRect(), NOT a scroll listener** — deliberately, to stay in step with Lenis. Core math: `travel = rect.height - innerHeight; progress = clamp(-rect.top / travel)`. Markup: outer `h-[250svh]` → `sticky top-0 h-svh overflow-hidden` → poster img + canvas + children. **This scroll-progress pattern is exactly what the construction sequence and interior walkthrough should reuse.**
- `components/hero/hero-canvas.tsx` + `hero-scene.tsx` (R3F, Environment preset="dawn", ACESFilmicToneMapping, 6 hardcoded BLOCKS, pointer parallax via `state.pointer.x` in useFrame) — **currently DEAD CODE, zero importers**. Working reference to revive/replace.
- `components/projects/master-plan-3d.tsx` (217 lines) is the ONLY live R3F scene. Canvas dpr=[1,1.5], OrbitControls (enablePan false, polar clamped, damping .08), materials+THREE.Color palette useMemo'd once, useFrame does ONLY `material.color.lerp(target, 0.12)` (docblock warns allocating THREE.Color in the frame loop causes stutter). Paired with keyboard-operable `<button aria-pressed>` tower list for a11y.
- `components/motion/fade-in-view.tsx`: **framer-motion IS used** (`import { m } from "framer-motion"`), ~40 call sites, manual stagger via `delay={index*0.05}`. `MotionProvider` = `<LazyMotion features={loadDomAnimation} strict>` — **`strict` means importing `motion` instead of `m` THROWS**.
- `components/motion/scroll-reveal.tsx`: the ONLY GSAP file. Dynamic `import("gsap")` + `import("gsap/ScrollTrigger")`, `gsap.context()` + `context.revert()` cleanup, `RevealLine` emits `[data-reveal-line]` for a `yPercent:110` masked slide, plus a 2500ms safety timer that force-completes if ScrollTrigger never fires. **Only ONE call site** (app/page.tsx:77-93). The `parallax` branch is unexercised.
- **GSAP and Lenis are NOT wired together** — no `lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update)`, no scrollerProxy. `LenisProvider` renders `null`, exposes NO instance (no context, no useLenis). Any scroll-linked 3D needs this plumbing added.
- `components/providers/reduced-motion-provider.tsx`: `useSyncExternalStore` with server snapshot `false`. **This is the hydration-safe storage pattern to copy for remembering the visitor's name.**

**Assets**: `/public` is 6.4MB — `frames/hero/001-036.webp` (4.7MB), `images/projects/*.webp` (16 files, 1.7MB), `panoramas/demo-interior.png` (only 1024×512 — far below the ~4096×2048 needed for a credible 360), `brochures/demo-brochure.pdf` (1KB stub). **ZERO .glb/.gltf/.hdr/.ktx2/.mp4/.webm anywhere.** `Environment preset="dawn"` fetches an HDRI from the drei CDN at runtime.

**Data model**:
- `lib/floor-plans.ts`: `Room = {name,x,y,w,h,share,kind}` on a unitless grid (kind: living|bedroom|kitchen|bath|utility|balcony); `FloorPlan = {id,label,width,height,rooms,entry:{x,y}}`. Four plans: 2bhk/3bhk/4bhk/5bhk. Helpers `getFloorPlan(bhk)`, `roomDimensions(room, carpetAreaSqFt)`, `compassRotation(facing)`, `vastuNote(facing)`. **This x/y/w/h grid is trivially extrudable to 3D walls/slabs — it is the natural source for the procedural interior.**
- `components/projects/progress-timeline.tsx` has `STAGE_FILL = {excavation:0.1, foundation:0.3, structure:0.6, finishing:0.85, handover:1}` — **already the site's canonical "how far up the building has got" scale; the natural driver for the construction sequence.**
- `lib/placeholders/projects.ts`: 12 projects. **All have `priceOnRequest:true`, `startingPrice` never set, `possession` never set, `specifications:[]`, `progress:[]`, `carpetAreaMin/Max:0`, `reraNumber:"AWAITING CLIENT"`.** Consequence: on the project page the Money/Specifications/Progress sections DO NOT RENDER today. `Unit` has an unused `floorPlanId?:string` hook. A `buildTower(id,name,floors,perFloor,soldThroughFloor)` factory synthesises units.
- `lib/types.ts` has `Project.progress[].stage` as the union matching STAGE_FILL.

**Storage/state**: Repo-wide grep for localStorage/sessionStorage/cookie found **exactly 3 hits, all in app/error.tsx** (a reload guard). No cookies, no `cookies()`, no persistence, no analytics. **Exactly one React context in the whole app** (ReducedMotionProvider). No zustand/jotai/redux. No auth, no personalization. 28 `"use client"` files of ~60 components.

**Layout tree** (app/layout.tsx): `<html>` → `<body flex min-h-full flex-col>` → JsonLd → ReducedMotionProvider → MotionProvider → [LenisProvider (renders null), skip link, SiteHeader, FestiveBanner, `<main id="main" className="flex-1 pb-16 lg:pb-0">`, SiteFooter, WhatsAppFab, StickyMobileActionBar]. **z-index ladder: SiteHeader z-50, StickyMobileActionBar z-50, skip-link focus z-[60], WhatsAppFab fixed.** A full-screen gate must exceed z-[60]. Next 16 uses globally-injected `LayoutProps<"/">` / `PageProps<"/projects/[slug]">` types (NOT imported) and `await params`.

**Governing spec**: `CLAUDE.md` §7 "WebGL/Three.js Guardrails" is a hard spec: PBR MeshStandardMaterial only, never flat unlit; no free-roam/jarring cuts (motion sickness) — dampened lerp / GSAP drone reveals; hero <100k tris, <30 draw calls, DPR ≤1.5; never allocate inside useFrame; pause rAF offscreen and on tab blur; dynamic ssr:false always; reserve dimensions via aspect-ratio to prevent CLS; **"Progressive enhancement is mandatory: real H1, body copy and links live in server-rendered HTML behind/around the canvas. Bots read HTML, not WebGL pixels."** §13 covers RERA §11(2)/§12/§59 + DPDP Act 2023 consent. `AGENTS.md` warns "This is NOT the Next.js you know — read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing App Router code."

**Comment style**: distinctive first-person engineering-rationale voice explaining *why*, often citing `CLAUDE.md §n`. Match it.

## What I need from you

A concrete, phased implementation architecture. Be specific about file paths, component boundaries, prop interfaces, and the order of work. Address in depth:

1. **Dark theme conversion strategy.** Given `.dark` is dead code and the target is a permanently-dark site (not a toggle): move `.dark` values into `:root` vs. add the class? What new elevation tokens (`--surface-1/2/3`) are needed? Give the concrete remap table for every raw brand class listed above, especially: what replaces `text-bronze` (64 uses, fails contrast), what replaces `bg-cream/50` (15 uses), and what replaces the `bg-charcoal`+`text-ivory` inversion device (20+36 uses). How to handle `site-header`'s collapsed two-state logic, the footer no longer separating, the invisible focus ring, the forest FAB, and the skip link. Recommend whether to do a mechanical find-replace or introduce a semantic layer.

2. **The onboarding gate architecture.** Where exactly does it mount in the layout tree? How does it avoid blocking SSR/SEO (bots must still get the full HTML — CLAUDE.md §7 is explicit)? How is "first visit" persisted given zero existing storage (design a hydration-safe `useSyncExternalStore` hook mirroring reduced-motion-provider)? What is the state machine (loading model → speaking → awaiting input → transitioning out)? How does the visitor's name propagate to the rest of the site (new context provider? where does it get consumed — header greeting? enquiry form prefill?)? DPDP consent implications of storing a name. How does it interact with Lenis (body scroll lock), the z-index ladder, and `SiteHeader`'s `overDarkHero` logic? What is the mobile/reduced-motion/no-WebGL fallback given `shouldRenderWebGL` refuses all mobile — design a relaxed gate function (e.g. `shouldRenderShowcaseWebGL`) and say precisely how it differs.

3. **The Ready Player Me avatar integration.** Concretely: how to obtain the GLB (the RPM avatar-creator URL flow, `?morphTargets=ARKit,Oculus%20Visemes` query param to get blendshapes, half-body vs full-body), where to store it, how to load it (`useGLTF` from drei — note drei is installed; do we need `meshoptimizer`/Draco config in next.config.ts?). How to implement: (a) **eye + head tracking of the mouse pointer** — the correct approach using the `RightEye`/`LeftEye`/`Head` bones and `Object3D.lookAt` with a damped target, clamped to plausible ranges so she doesn't snap her neck; (b) **lip-sync to the pre-recorded MP3s** — the practical approaches (Web Audio `AnalyserNode` amplitude → drive `viseme_aa`/`jawOpen` morph, vs. a pre-baked viseme timeline JSON), recommend one and justify; (c) idle animation (blinking via `eyeBlinkLeft/Right` morphs on a randomised timer, subtle breathing/sway), and whether to use Mixamo animation clips retargeted onto the RPM rig. Name the exact morph target names.

4. **Voice production + playback.** The exact script lines to record. File layout under `/public/audio/`. How playback is triggered given **browsers block autoplay of audio without a user gesture** — this is the single biggest UX trap in the whole feature; design the interaction that satisfies autoplay policy (e.g. an "Enter" / unmute affordance) without feeling like a dead-end. How to sync the lip-sync analyser to the `<audio>`/Web Audio graph. Captions/transcript for accessibility and for users who decline audio.

5. **The procedural construction sequence.** Geometry design: how to build a credible tower from code (core, columns, slabs, facade panels, glazing, crown) using InstancedMesh, and how many instances. How scroll progress maps to construction stages using the existing `STAGE_FILL` ramp. The camera choreography (a drone-like orbit/rise, damped, per CLAUDE.md's no-free-roam rule). Where it mounts (replace `HomeHero`'s frame sequence, or a new section below it?) and what happens to the now-orphaned `hero-canvas.tsx`/`hero-scene.tsx` and the 4.7MB of frame WebPs. How to wire scroll progress — reuse `scroll-frame-sequence`'s rAF+getBoundingClientRect pattern, or introduce GSAP ScrollTrigger properly wired to Lenis? Recommend one and say why. Materials/lighting to hit "premium dark" (Environment HDRI choice given the CDN dependency, tone mapping, whether to add @react-three/postprocessing for bloom/vignette/grain — it's specified in CLAUDE.md §4 but NOT installed).

6. **The scrollable 3D apartment interior.** How to extrude `lib/floor-plans.ts` rooms into walls/floor/ceiling. Camera path design (a spline through rooms driven by scroll, damped, no free-roam). Furniture — procedural primitives or nothing? Lighting for interiors (area lights via drei, baked-look). Where it mounts on `/projects/[slug]` — does it replace the `PannellumTour` section (whose 1024×512 panorama is inadequate anyway) or sit alongside? How it relates to the existing `FloorPlanViewer` (which stays as the accessible/crawlable twin, mirroring the MasterPlan/UnitMatrix precedent).

7. **Mouse-following behaviour beyond the avatar** ("nice models which follow mouse pointer") — a reusable damped pointer-parallax hook usable across scenes, building on the existing `state.pointer` usage in hero-scene.tsx.

8. **Dependencies to add** and any `next.config.ts` changes required (GLB/GLTF handling, transpilePackages, etc.). Be precise about what's genuinely needed vs. nice-to-have.

9. **Phasing.** A concrete ordered sequence of phases where each phase leaves the site in a working, reviewable state. Note the user wants to see the transformed home page early.

10. **Risks and honest trade-offs.** Call out specifically: the uncanny-valley risk, the autoplay-policy trap, the mobile story (the user wants maximum visual quality but half of India's real-estate traffic is mobile), what breaks SEO/RERA compliance if done carelessly, the ~200-class dark remap being genuinely tedious, and that the user said to ignore performance but CLAUDE.md §7 mandates a lot of it — how to reconcile those two.

Return a detailed technical plan I can turn into an execution document. Prefer specificity (file paths, function signatures, exact morph-target names, exact token values) over generality.

## 4. Tech Stack (all free / open-source)

- **Next.js 16** (App Router, TypeScript, React 19, Server Components by default, Turbopack).
  Typed routes are on by default — a `<Link>` to a route that does not exist fails the build,
  so stub pages must land before the links that point at them.
- **Tailwind CSS v4** + **shadcn/ui** (Radix primitives)
- **Framer Motion** (component reveals and micro-interactions) + **GSAP 3.13+** with ScrollTrigger
  (scroll-linked headline reveals) + **Lenis** (smooth scroll).
  Framer must be used through `LazyMotion` with the `domAnimation` feature set and the `m`
  primitive, never the full `motion` component — the difference is roughly 150–300ms of blocking
  time on pages carrying a dozen reveals. `components/motion/motion-provider.tsx` sets `strict`
  so a stray `motion` import fails loudly.
  - GSAP is **100% free since 30 Apr 2025** (Webflow announcement), including all former Club plugins,
    commercial use covered. No paid dependency remains in the motion stack.
- **React Three Fiber** + `@react-three/drei` + `@react-three/postprocessing` (tasteful WebGL only)
- **Embla Carousel** (galleries), **react-hook-form + Zod** (forms), **schema-dts** (typed JSON-LD)
- **Sanity CMS** (projects/units/amenities/locations/testimonials/blog), Studio embedded at `/studio`.
  Alternative: Payload v3 (self-host). Sanity recommended for a non-technical builder team.
- Email: **Resend** (fallback Nodemailer). Spam: **Cloudflare Turnstile** + honeypot

## 6. Design System — "Quiet Luxury"

### Color (60-30-10)
```
--charcoal:   #141414    --charcoal-2: #1A1A1A    --ivory: #F5F1E8    --cream: #EDE7DA
--gold:       #B99C6B    --bronze:     #8C6A3F    --forest: #243B34
--grey:       #6B6B6B    --grey-2:     #9A9A9A
```
- **60% ground:** warm off-whites / ivory / stone grey / deep charcoal — let architecture dominate.
- **30% structural:** rich navy `#0A192F`, dark emerald `#043927` / forest `#243B34`, stone grey.
  Burgundy/plum optional for moody editorial.
- **10% accent:** muted metallics only — champagne/muted gold `#D4AF37`, soft bronze `#CD7F32`.
  Never saturated primaries, neon, or chaotic gradients (they read as *discount*).
- **Gold-on-charcoal small text must pass WCAG AA 4.5:1** — lighten to `#C9AE7C`+ if needed.
- **Bronze-on-ivory small text likewise.** Measured: `#8C6A3F` on `#F5F1E8` is 4.28:1 and fails.
  The implementation ships `#7A5A33` (5.5:1) as `--bronze`; use it for eyebrows and captions.

### Typography
- **Max two families.** Display serif = **Fraunces** (variable, Google Fonts) or Playfair Display /
  Cormorant. Body/UI = **Manrope** or **Inter**. Gujarati/Hindi = Noto Sans Gujarati / Devanagari.
- Self-host via `next/font` (subset). Fontshare fonts (Satoshi, General Sans) are free but under ITF
  EULA — **use their API, do not self-host without consent**.
- Type scale (1.25): **12, 14, 16 (base), 20, 25, 31, 39, 49, 61 px**. Line-height 1.5 body / 1.1 display.
- Generous letter-spacing (`tracking-widest`) on small uppercase nav/subheads — utility `.eyebrow`.
- Body line length constrained to **50–75 characters** (`max-w-prose`).
- Never system defaults (Arial) or decorative scripts.

### Space & geometry
- Spacing scale (4px base): 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128. Grid: 12-col, max-w 1440px.
- **Whitespace is the luxury.** Double or triple template-standard margins (`py-24`, `gap-16`).
- **Every element aligns to the grid.** A 2–3px misalignment shatters the precision illusion.
- Radius restrained 2–8px. Elevation soft and low-contrast — prefer 1px borders + tonal shifts
  over heavy shadows.

### Imagery
- No cheap staged stock — HNW buyers detect it instantly. Artistic, candid, unique crops, dramatic
  architectural angles.
- **Color-grade all assets as one system** (identical lighting, shadow depth, temperature).
- If an image adds no emotional or informational value, delete it and leave negative space. Let images
  breathe; never edge-to-edge collages.
- Copy sells lifestyle, status and neighbourhood culture — minimal, sophisticated, zero hype. Lead
  with brand philosophy before dumping listings.

### Motion tokens
- Micro 150–200ms · UI 250–350ms · section reveals 400–600ms. **Never exceed 500ms** for interface
  animation; snappy beats slow.
- Easings: entrance `cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)`; transition `cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)`;
  Framer default `[0.25,0.1,0.25,1]`.
- Animate composite properties only (opacity, transform) → 60fps.
- GSAP ScrollTrigger for pinned/scroll-linked sequences + SplitText headline reveals; Framer Motion
  for component/page micro-interactions; Lenis (lerp ~0.1); View Transitions API for routes where
  supported.
- **Always honor `prefers-reduced-motion`** — disable Lenis, reduce GSAP to ≤300ms fades. Disable
  smooth scroll on touch if INP suffers.
- Converts: scroll-linked reveals, parallax within masks, horizontal galleries, sticky section
  transitions, tasteful text-mask reveals. Avoid: gimmicky cursors, motion that delays content,
  autoplay audio, chaotically spinning 3D models.

### Accessibility
WCAG 2.1 AA contrast, keyboard nav, visible focus, form labels, alt text, reduced-motion respected.

---

## 7. WebGL / Three.js Guardrails

Treat the viewport as a cinematic film set, not a toy.

- **Materials:** PBR `MeshStandardMaterial` with real roughness/metalness/normal maps (e.g.
  metalness 0.8 / roughness 0.2). Never flat unlit meshes.
- **Lighting:** architectural-studio setup — soft ambient occlusion, subtle directional light with
  shadow mapping (`<ambientLight intensity={0.5} />` + `<directionalLight castShadow />`).
- **Post-processing:** subtle SSR, controlled bloom, chromatic aberration, film grain, vignette.
- **Camera:** no jarring cuts or free-roam (motion sickness). Dampened lerp / GSAP drone-like reveals.
- **Budgets:** hero scene <100k triangles, <30 draw calls; DPR capped at 1.5.
- **Assets:** Draco/meshopt-compressed GLTF; KTX2 or WebP textures (GPU-direct, no CPU decode).
- **Memory:** never allocate inside `useFrame`/rAF (`new THREE.Vector3()` → GC stutter). Instantiate
  vectors/matrices once and recycle. Pause rAF when offscreen (IntersectionObserver) and on tab blur.
- **Threading:** offload the Three.js pipeline to a Web Worker via **OffscreenCanvas** so shader
  compilation/geometry parsing never blocks the main thread (keeps INP <200ms).
- **Loading:** wrap `<Canvas>` in `dynamic(() => import(...), { ssr:false })` — never block LCP.
  Reserve container dimensions with CSS `aspect-ratio` to prevent CLS.
- **Fallbacks:** mobile / low-power / reduced-motion get a high-res static WebP or `<video poster>`
  instead of the 3D scene.
- **Progressive enhancement is mandatory:** real H1, body copy and links live in server-rendered HTML
  behind/around the canvas. Bots read HTML, not WebGL pixels.

---

## 8. Page-by-Page Spec

content.text:
I read the specific files needed to confirm the token indirection, the gate pattern, the scroll math, the layout tree and CLAUDE.md §4/§6/§7. Below is the architecture. --- # 3D / Dark-Theme Overhaul — Implementation Architecture --- ## 0. The one structural insight that shapes everything `app/globals.css` uses `@theme inline`, so every `--color-*` is a *pointer* to a raw var on `:root`. That means **the majority of the "~200 raw brand class occurrences" convert by editing five hex values, not by touching 200 lines of TSX.** I built the whole Phase 1 plan around that. Details in §1. Second insight: `lib/webgl.ts`'s docblock says *"Every 3D surface on this site is decoration layered over content that already works, so the bar for mounting one is deliberately high."* That premise is now false for three surfaces. The gate function must fork, not be loosened — see §2.6. --- ## 1. Dark theme conversion ### 1.1 `:root` vs `.dark` — do both, but `:root` is the source of truth Move the dark values into `:root`. Keep `` as well. Reasons, in order: 1. `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *))` matches *descendants* of `.dark`. `` is not its own descendant, so tokens declared only in `.dark` would not apply to rules targeting `html` itself. Putting values in `:root` sidesteps that entirely. 2. Two live token blocks means the next author edits the wrong one. One block, one truth. 3. Still add the class, because `tw-animate-css`, Radix and any future shadcn component ship `dark:` variants that only fire inside `.dark`. Cheap insurance, zero cost. 4. Redefine `.dark { }` as an **empty block with a comment** explaining it is intentionally inert now — deleting it would make the `@custom-variant` line look orphaned. Do **not** add `suppressHydrationWarning` — there is no theme toggle, so nothing mutates `class` before hydration. (The onboarding script mutates `data-onboarding`, a different attribute React does not own.) ### 1.2 New tokens The critical decision: **the page ground must become darker than `--charcoal`.** Today `--charcoal #141414` is both the darkest brand value and the "inverted emphasis" surface. If `--background: var(--charcoal)`, you have nothing left to raise things *onto*, and `site-footer` (already charcoal) stops separating from `main` — exactly the risk you flagged. Introduce `--ink` below charcoal and the whole elevation system falls out. Warm-neutral ramp, aligned to `#2a2622` which `hero-scene.tsx` already uses — evidence the original designer had already picked a warm dark: ```css :root { /* --- Elevation ramp. Dark UIs express elevation as lightness, not shadow; CLAUDE.md §6 already prefers tonal shifts + 1px borders over shadows. --- */ --ink: #0f0e0d; /* page ground. Nothing is darker. */ --surface-1: #141414; /* = --charcoal. Footer, sticky bars. */ --surface-2: #1a1917; /* cards, alternating sections */ --surface-3: #22201d; /* popovers, hover, the emphasis plinth */ --surface-4: #2a2622; /* deepest raise; matches hero-scene's existing warm dark */ --hairline: rgb(245 241 232 / 10%); --hairline-strong: rgb(245 241 232 / 18%); --hairline-gold: color-mix(in oklab, var(--gold) 34%, transparent); } ``` ### 1.3 Retuned raw palette — this is where the 140 free conversions come from ```css --charcoal: #141414; /* unchanged */ --charcoal-2: #1a1917; /* warmed one step to join the ramp */ --ivory: #f5f1e8; /* unchanged — still the body colour */ --cream: #ede7da; /* unchanged, but now only legal on gold/ivory grounds */ --gold: #b99c6b; /* unchanged. 7.5:1 on --ink */ --gold-soft: #c9ae7c; /* unchanged. 9.5:1 on --ink */ /* INVERTED RATIONALE. The old comment darkened bronze from #8C6A3F to #7A5A33 to clear 4.5:1 against ivory. The ground is now ink, so the same requirement pushes the other way: #7A5A33 measures 1.9:1 on charcoal. #A4906A measures 6.2:1 on --ink and 5.2:1 on --surface-3, so all 64 `text-bronze` eyebrows, `focus:border-bronze`, `accent-[var(--bronze)]` and the active map marker clear AA without a single class edit. */ --bronze: #a4906a; /* #243B34 is 1.5:1 on ink — the WhatsApp FAB and its ring vanish, and the `available` unit cell stops reading as green. Lifting the token fixes the FAB, the ring glow and the availability stack in one edit. */ --forest: #2f6b53; --forest-deep: #243b34; /* retained for any surface that wants the old value */ --navy: #0a192f; /* still unused in the DOM — now reserved for WebGL fog/env */ --stone: #6b6b6b; /* 2.9:1 on ink — DEMOTE: borders/decoration only, never text */ --stone-2: #9a9a9a; /* 6.9:1 on ink — the muted text colour */ ``` Add to `@theme inline`: `--color-ink`, `--color-surface-1..4`, `--color-forest-deep`. ### 1.4 Semantic block ```css --background: var(--ink); --foreground: var(--ivory); --card: var(--surface-2); --card-foreground: var(--ivory); --popover: var(--surface-3); --popover-foreground: var(--ivory); --primary: var(--gold); /* CTAs go gold on dark; charcoal buttons vanish */ --primary-foreground: var(--charcoal); --secondary: var(--surface-3); --secondary-foreground: var(--ivory); --muted: var(--surface-2); --muted-foreground: var(--stone-2); --accent: var(--gold-soft); --accent-foreground: var(--charcoal); --destructive: #e08585; /* the dead .dark block's #c96a6a is only 4.4:1 on surface-3 */ --border: var(--hairline); --input: var(--hairline-strong); --ring: var(--gold-soft); color-scheme: dark; /* dark scrollbars, form controls, `, ``, `

` caption region, `

` transcript, "Skip introduction" button, mute toggle. `role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby`. Focus to the input on `awaiting-name`; `Escape` = skip. --- ## 4. Voice production + playback ### 4.1 The script Four lines, four files (so one can be re-recorded without redoing all), ~16s total. The gate is a toll booth; every extra second raises bounce. | file | text | ~len | |---|---|---| | `line-01-greeting.mp3` | "Hello, and welcome to {Brand}. I'm Aanya — I look after guests here." | 4.5s | | `line-02-ask-name.mp3` | "Before we begin — what should I call you?" | 3.5s | | `line-03-thanks.mp3` | "Wonderful. Let me show you what we've been building." | 3.5s | | `line-04-nudge.mp3` | "Whenever you're ready — just your first name." | 3.0s | **The name cannot be spoken, and that is a design decision, not a limitation.** Pre-recorded audio can't say an arbitrary name; a splice pipeline means recording hundreds of Indian first names, and mispronouncing someone's name is worse than not saying it. Resolution: **line-03 is deliberately name-free and plays while the caption area types "Lovely to meet you, {Name}."** The visual carries the personalisation, the voice carries the warmth. Write this rationale into `script.md`. Also, per §10.4: **her script contains zero factual claims about any project.** An AI presenter making project claims is an advertisement by an unregistered agent under RERA. Keep it a greeting. ### 4.2 File layout ``` public/audio/onboarding/ line-01-greeting.mp3 line-01-greeting.visemes.json line-02-ask-name.mp3 line-02-ask-name.visemes.json line-03-thanks.mp3 line-03-thanks.visemes.json line-04-nudge.mp3 line-04-nudge.visemes.json script.md LICENSE.md lib/onboarding-script.ts // [{ id, src, cuesSrc, text, durationHint }] — one array so // audio, captions and viseme tracks can never drift apart ``` ElevenLabs settings: one consistent voice (Indian-English accent if available), stability ~0.45, similarity ~0.8. Export **128 kbps mono 44.1 kHz** (mono halves the file; the timeline doesn't care). Normalise to ~−16 LUFS. **Trim leading silence to zero** or the lip-sync appears late. ### 4.3 Autoplay — the trap, and the design that dodges it Every browser blocks `audio.play()` without a prior gesture on the origin. Chrome's Media Engagement Index can grant an exception on repeat visits — which is precisely the case that never happens here, since the gate is first-visit-only.
